scams.name: Rhodes Old Town Bar Bill Extortion
scams.description: Rhodes Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage medieval city, and its Sokratous Street and Socratous Square are lined with bars and tavernas catering to tourists. In June 2025, Greek Herald ran 'Rhodes Old Town bars slammed for overcharging tourists' (2025-06-19), and the Daily Mail followed with 'Popular Greek tourist resort labelled the ultimate rip-off for drinks' (2025-06-06) and 'Inside the rip-off holiday haven fleecing Brit tourists' (2025-06-28). The pattern documented across these 2025 news pieces: tourists walk into Old Town bars, order 'normal' drinks, and receive bills of €40–€80 per drink. r/Rhodes 'Old Town scams' (comments/1lnk2ib) captures the community view: 'Be aware of the overcharging tactics and other scams of some unprofessional people who only look after profit.' r/CasualUK 'I wonder if being served a full sized glass Welly of lager' (comments/14omz07) documents a specific variant: bars serve drinks in oversized 'novelty glasses' that look like a pint but actually hold two or three pints, then charge per pint at the inflated rate. Combined with no menu visibility ('I had one of these in the old town in a bar with no prices on the menu'), the final bill regularly reaches €150+ for what felt like a normal drink round. r/Rhodes 'As a Greek, it's embarrassing how much of a tourist trap' (comments/1dezzu4) captures local frustration: 'Even when looking at the reviews online afterwards, everyone rated it 1-star as a rip off.' Your protection: before sitting at any Rhodes Old Town bar, verify the printed drink menu has posted prices. Walk out immediately if the bar cannot produce one. Pay per drink at the bar rather than running a tab. If served a drink in an unusual 'novelty glass,' confirm the price before drinking — 'novelty' is often the euphemism for the rip-off volume. Travel in groups for Old Town evenings; the bar staff are less aggressive with groups than with solo visitors. Daily Mail June 2025 reporting confirmed that Rhodes authorities have begun fining named bars, but enforcement is reactive rather than preventive. For legitimate Old Town dining, community-recommended options with posted prices include Nireas Restaurant, Hatzikelis, and To Meltemi — all with 4.4+ Google ratings.
scams.avoidance: Verify the printed drink menu has posted prices before sitting — walk out if none is produced Pay per drink at the bar rather than a running tab Confirm the price of any drink served in an unusual 'novelty glass' before drinking Travel in groups for Old Town evenings — staff are less aggressive with groups Community-recommended posted-price Old Town dining: Nireas, Hatzikelis, To Meltemi (all 4.4+ ratings)
scams.location: Rhodes Old Town (Medieval City), Socratous Street bars, Sokratous square nightlife

scams.name: Rhodes Cruise Port & Airport Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Rhodes is a major Mediterranean cruise destination, and Kolona Harbour (the main cruise dock adjacent to the Old Town) sees multiple large ships most summer days. Cruise passengers step off the ship and face a fleet of taxis quoting €40 to Lindos (real metered fare €55–€70 one-way over 50 kilometres, which is a reasonable price) or €25 to Faliraki (real fare €15–€20) or €15 to Rhodes Old Town (walkable in 5 minutes). r/Rhodes 'Rhodes Busses and Taxi Fares' (comments/1hanqw2) gives the defensive rule: 'Make sure to agree upon the price before entering, to avoid scammers who try to overcharge tourists.' r/GreeceTravel 'Was I fooled by this taxi driver? Paid 160 Euros' (comments/1ghxrhm) documents a Rhodes-parallel taxi overcharge case. Diagoras Airport (RHO) taxi overcharges mirror the Athens pattern: drivers claim the meter is broken, quote €40 for the 14-kilometre ride to Old Town (real fare €25–€30 metered), or take a padded route through the suburbs. Older travellers transferring to resort hotels in Ixia or Faliraki should be aware that many resort-area taxi stands operate as cartels where drivers refuse discount apps like FreeNow — meaning a €25 metered run to your Ixia hotel may require walking to the main road before a legitimate taxi will accept the fare. Your protection: from Kolona Harbour, walk to Rhodes Old Town (5 minutes) rather than taking a taxi. For the airport run, use FreeNow or Beat apps for regulated fares. The KTEL bus from Diagoras Airport to Rhodes city centre is €2.40 per person and runs every 30–60 minutes — slower (30–45 minutes) but eliminates taxi exposure entirely. For Lindos day trips from Rhodes town, the KTEL bus costs €5.50 and runs every 30 minutes in peak season; the drive is 55 minutes each way. Cruise passengers pressed for time should consider the cruise line's official Lindos shore excursion (overpriced but honestly priced) rather than a roadside taxi deal. Save Tourist Police 171 for disputes; they have Rhodes offices and respond to documented overcharges.
scams.avoidance: Walk from Kolona Harbour to Rhodes Old Town — it is 5 minutes on foot From Diagoras Airport, use KTEL bus (€2.40, 30–45 min to city) or FreeNow/Beat apps For Lindos day trips, KTEL bus is €5.50 and runs every 30 min in peak season At resort hotel driveways, walk to the main road if cartel taxis refuse app pickups Cruise passengers with tight timing should consider the cruise line's Lindos shore excursion
scams.location: Rhodes cruise port (Kolona Harbour), Diagoras Airport (RHO) rank, Mandraki Harbour taxi rank

scams.name: Lindos Acropolis Donkey Ride & ATV Rental Damage
scams.description: Lindos is a whitewashed hilltop village topped by the Acropolis of Lindos — one of Greece's most beautiful archaeological sites. The approach from the village to the Acropolis involves a steep 10-minute walk up switchback stone paths, and donkey rides are offered at the trailhead for €5–€10 per rider. The scam variant follows the Santorini playbook: handlers quote a low price at the bottom, then demand €15–€30 mid-ascent 'because of your weight' or 'because the donkey is tired.' r/VirginVoyages 'Greek island glow for honeymoon' (comments/1jw9guw) flags the animal welfare concern: 'The other option is a donkey ride, but the donkeys are not treated…' — the same ethical framework as Santorini applies, with documented spinal injuries to overworked donkeys. For Faliraki and Rhodes city ATV rentals, the damage deposit pattern matches Heraklion: shops take €300–€500 cash deposit, 'discover' scratches on return, and charge five to ten times the real repair cost. r/Rhodes community threads consistently warn about ATV rentals in Faliraki's party strip where operators rotate storefront names seasonally. Car rental in Rhodes has similar issues; reputable agencies are Avis, Budget, Hertz, and Europcar at Diagoras Airport rather than Rhodes town storefronts. Your protection: for Lindos, walk the 10 minutes to the Acropolis — the path is steep but the views on the way up are part of the experience. If mobility is a real concern, consider visiting Lindos on a cruise excursion that uses golf carts for transfers within the village. Do not ride the donkeys — both for animal welfare reasons and to avoid the mid-ascent price-hike scam. For ATVs, skip rentals entirely in Faliraki; rent cars from major international brands at Diagoras Airport. Photograph every panel of any rental vehicle before departure with timestamps. Pay by credit card for chargeback leverage on fake damage claims.
scams.avoidance: Walk the 10-minute Lindos Acropolis path — the views are part of the experience For mobility-impaired visitors, cruise excursions with golf-cart transfers are the ethical alternative Do not ride Lindos donkeys — both mid-ascent price hikes and documented welfare issues Rent cars from Avis, Budget, Hertz, Europcar at Diagoras Airport — not Rhodes town storefronts Photograph every panel of any vehicle rental before departure and pay by credit card for chargeback
scams.location: Lindos village access path, Lindos Acropolis donkey route, Faliraki ATV rental shops

scams.name: Faliraki 'All-Inclusive' Bar & Tourist-Strip Overcharge
scams.description: Faliraki is Rhodes's main package-holiday resort town — designated, as r/greece 'Holiday booked in August for a small town outside Rhodes' (comments/1cq58u5) puts it, 'for tourists. Imagine that in the winter time is dead, it's a village made for tourists.' r/Rhodes 'Hello! Planning on vacation' (comments/19d3ryd) summarises: 'Why Faliraki? It's only a tourist trap.' The area's bars and restaurants use the classic cruise-strip pattern: 'all-inclusive' deals with small print, inflated cocktail prices once you are seated, and 'entertainment' surcharges on bills. A specific Faliraki scam: 'VIP bottle service' packages that advertise €80 per person for a bottle of spirits plus mixers and table reservation, but on checkout produce a bill with 'table fee €200,' 'service €80,' 'VIP security €40,' and an inflated spirit price. r/Rhodes 'Avoiding Tourist Trap Restaurants and Souvenir Shops?' (comments/1skzr54) captures the scale: 'I think local restaurant I could get two entrees and two drinks for $30 or so. But the tourist traps usually will run $80 to $100 for the same amount of stuff.' Ixia and Kolymbia resort areas run similar patterns: shops near the beach charge €15 for ice cream that is €3 in Rhodes Town. Your protection: for a reliable Rhodes holiday experience, stay in Rhodes Town or in Lindos village rather than Faliraki — both have more local character and better-priced dining. If you are at a Faliraki package hotel, eat at the hotel's main restaurant (where prices are included in your package) rather than the bar strip. For independent dining, ask your hotel's front desk for locally-recommended non-tourist tavernas and confirm prices in writing. Cover charges and minimum consumptions are legally required to be posted in Greece; refuse any bar that cannot produce printed price documentation. Pay by credit card for chargeback leverage. For day trips to Lindos or Rhodes Town from Faliraki, use the KTEL bus (€4.50 per person) rather than the taxi cartel at the beach strip.
scams.avoidance: Stay in Rhodes Town or Lindos village rather than Faliraki — better food, more local character At Faliraki package hotels, eat at the main restaurant where prices are included in your package For independent dining, ask the hotel front desk for locally-recommended tavernas with posted prices Refuse any bar that cannot produce printed cover-charge / minimum-consumption documentation Use KTEL bus (€4.50) for Faliraki → Rhodes Town or Lindos — avoid beach strip taxi cartel
scams.location: Faliraki main bar strip, 'Bar Street' Faliraki, Kolymbia and Ixia resort-area tourist shops

scams.name: Old Town Tourist-Menu Restaurant Overcharge
scams.description: Inside Rhodes Old Town's medieval walls, restaurants along the main tourist spine on Sokratous Street and near the Grand Master's Palace use the tourist-menu playbook: menus posted outside with one price, menus at the table with another, welcome bread and olives billed as cover charges, and fish priced per kilogram. r/Rhodes 'Avoiding Tourist Trap Restaurants and Souvenir Shops?' (comments/1skzr54) provides the pricing benchmark: 'I think local restaurant I could get two entrees and two drinks for $30 or so. But the tourist traps usually will run $80 to $100 for the same amount of stuff.' A 2.5–3x tourist markup is the standard. The Daily Mail's June 2025 investigation 'Inside the rip-off holiday haven fleecing Brit tourists' named specific Old Town restaurants engaging in menu substitution — tourists are shown one menu at the door and billed from a different menu at the table. Tourist Police in Rhodes have fined several venues in 2025, but the practice continues across the approximately 80 restaurants inside the Old Town walls. The older-traveller-specific concern is that cruise passengers and guided-tour groups often eat at the first convenient restaurant on their itinerary — tour guides sometimes receive commission on this, making 'recommended' restaurants a potential conflict of interest. Your protection: confirm prices match between the outside menu and the table menu before sitting. Refuse welcome bread, olives, tzatziki when they arrive — Greek law requires cover charges to be posted and prohibits unlisted additions (see r/GreeceTravel 'Another day, another illegal bread charge on my bill' comments/1531tjz). Count the bill line by line and dispute any non-ordered items. For genuinely good Old Town dining with posted transparent prices, community recommendations include Nireas Restaurant, Hatzikelis (old Turkish fountain setting), To Meltemi, and Alexis Palace — all have 4.4+ Google ratings and 500+ reviews. For lunch during a cruise excursion, walk inland toward the Municipal Market on Socratous Square or north toward Pythagora Street where local tavernas serve residents at half the Old Town tourist prices.
scams.avoidance: Confirm the outside menu matches the table menu before sitting — walk out otherwise Refuse welcome bread, olives, tzatziki — Greek law prohibits unlisted cover charges (€500 fines) Count the bill line by line and dispute non-ordered items Community-recommended posted-price Old Town: Nireas, Hatzikelis, To Meltemi, Alexis Palace (4.4+ ratings) For lunch during a cruise excursion, walk inland to Pythagora Street for local tavernas at half the price
scams.location: Rhodes Old Town (Medieval City), restaurants inside the walls near Sokratous, near Dodecanese Palace

scams.name: Old Town 'Fake Market' Counterfeit & Bracelet Distraction
scams.description: Rhodes Old Town has a 'fake market' zone on and around Sokratous Street where shops sell counterfeit designer goods — bags, sunglasses, watches — at €30–€150. r/Rhodes 'Rhodes Old Town & Hotels' (comments/1l11j2d) mentions this directly: 'I have heard that there should be a fake market Selling copies of designer brands in Old Town Rhodes? Is that true?' EU customs law allows seizure at UK and US borders of knowingly-purchased counterfeit items, and returning travellers have had items confiscated at Heathrow and JFK with no recourse. Unknowingly-purchased items are typically only seized (not prosecuted), but you lose the item and the cash. A parallel scam targets older travellers specifically: bracelet-and-flower distraction teams operate at the Mandraki Harbour entrance, around the Grand Master's Palace, and at the main Old Town gate (Eleftherias Gate). The mechanic mirrors Athens Syntagma — one team member places a bracelet or flower, a partner 'confirms' it, and a third member blocks the escape. r/GreeceTravel bracelet warning threads apply directly: in 2025 these crews expanded from Athens/Thessaloniki to Rhodes Old Town during peak season (June–September). Your protection: do not buy counterfeit designer goods — the customs risk is real and the items are typically worthless substitutes. For genuine Rhodes souvenirs, look for handmade ceramics at Icons Art Studio or Paradise Ceramics on Sokratous Street (marked provenance), local olive oil from Kodylas or Crete-imported Sitia Co-op brands, or handmade leather goods at Apollon Leather workshops. For the bracelet/flower teams, cross your arms and step back immediately when approached; do not engage in conversation. Keep your wallet in a front zipped pocket or a crossbody bag worn in front when walking through Old Town. Report persistent crews to Tourist Police 171 — Rhodes has an active Old Town Tourist Police post at the Eleftherias Gate during summer months.
scams.avoidance: Do not buy counterfeit designer goods — UK/US customs will seize at borders, no recourse For genuine souvenirs: Icons Art Studio or Paradise Ceramics (ceramics), Apollon Leather (leather) Cross arms and step back if anyone approaches with a bracelet or flower Keep wallet in front zipped pocket or crossbody bag worn in front in Old Town Report persistent crews to Tourist Police 171 — active post at Eleftherias Gate in summer
scams.location: Rhodes Old Town (Medieval City) market streets, Sokratous Street souvenir shops, Mandraki Harbour
